# Working with AI: the conventions

<!-- generated by agentkit: replaced on upgrade. The project's own rules go in AGENTS.md outside the agentkit section; where they disagree, the project's rules win. -->

These conventions are the same for every agent: Claude Code, Codex, Kimi, Grok, DeepSeek or any other. The commands below are written as `python3 .agentkit/agentkit.py …`, so any agent that can run commands can use them.

## The task card is the only memory

Chat history gets lost: a new session, a new agent or a new person, and it is gone. So the requirement, what people have decided and how far the work has got all live in the task card (`tasks.dir` in `agentkit.toml`, by default `docs/tasks/<task-id>.md`).

- Before you start, run `task show` and read the whole card before you touch anything.
- Before you stop, update the status in Steps and the Handoff, then run `task handoff --agent <which agent you are>`.
- Commit the task card together with the code.

## The rhythm of the work

1. **Restate first**: write the requirement into the task card in your own words (who needs it / what it solves / done when), list the decisions for people and suggest the steps, then stop (`prompt restate`).
2. **Wait for a person to confirm**: "Confirmed by" is filled in only by a person running `task confirm` in their own terminal. Until the requirement is confirmed, change no file other than the task card. If the requirement changes after it was confirmed, the sign-off is void and a person must confirm again.
3. **Reproduce first**: before fixing a bug or changing business behavior, write a failing test, run it and show the output, then ask whether you may start on the change (`prompt repro`).
4. **One step at a time**: do one item of Steps at a time. When it is done, stop, report what you did and what the evidence is, and update that item's status.
5. **Evidence comes from the tools**: use the real output of `checks` as evidence; never write results by hand or make them up (`prompt verify`).
6. **3 rounds at most**: if the same problem is still not right after 3 rounds of changes, stop, explain where you are stuck, and suggest another approach or a smaller step instead of pushing on.
7. **Hand off before you stop** (`prompt handoff`).

## What to ask people

- Do not decide these yourself; put them under "Decisions for people" in the task card with your suggestion: changing a shared module or making a local change, external interfaces and how errors are reported, text users can see, database schemas, permissions.
- When a person decides something in the conversation, record the decision, who made it and the date in the task card, so the next person or agent can see it.
- If the requirement is missing any of the three questions, say so directly and ask before you carry on.

## Boundaries

- Change only code within the scope of the requirement. List other problems you notice along the way; do not fix them in passing.
- Protected paths cannot be changed. When you are blocked, stop, explain why the change is needed and let a person decide; do not look for a way around it.
- Do not commit, push or change remote permissions unless a person clearly says you may.
- Do not skip git hooks (`--no-verify`), and never run `task confirm` for a person.

## Before you commit

- Review in a new session: `/selfcheck` in Claude Code, or run `review` to have the configured reviewers each review in a fresh session.
- Write the PR description with `prompt pr-desc`, with the task id on the first line.

## Commands side by side

| Step | Claude Code | Other agents that can run commands |
|---|---|---|
| Read the task card | shown when the session starts | `task show` |
| Restate the requirement | `/restate` | `prompt restate "<requirement>"` |
| Write a failing test | `/repro` | `prompt repro` |
| Run the checks for evidence | `/verify` | `checks` |
| Review your own change | `/selfcheck` (new session) | `review` |
| Write the PR description | `/pr-desc` | `prompt pr-desc` |
| Hand off | `/handoff` | `prompt handoff`, then `task handoff` |

Chat-only bots without repository access: a person runs `prompt start` or another step, pastes the whole output to the bot, and copies the answer into the task card.

## Project facts

Run `python3 .agentkit/agentkit.py context` to see this repository's check commands, protected paths and high-risk paths.

## Rules from corrections

These go in AGENTS.md, outside the agentkit section. That part belongs to the project, every agent reads it, and upgrading the kit never overwrites it.
